Doc/comment/rules pass done — not a token sweep this time but a re-read of what the prose **claims**, which is where the old model actually lived. Four of those claims turned out to be live defects, not stale wording.

## The defects

1. **The queue's session instructions never captured.** The slot executor's did; the port lost the step. Every unattended session ends by having its container reclaimed — the ending no `SessionEnd` fires on — so no transcript reached the logs branch. The growth lifecycle's conversation half had nothing to mine and the usage fold's task-status census counted nothing, both reporting healthy over an empty input. Restored; `engine-tests/scheduler/queue/instructions.test.mjs` fails when the step is removed.

2. **Bootstrap wired a label-fired routine and no invocation endpoint at all.** A repo adopted from that text would have a queue that fills and hands nothing off. Rewritten as the two halves it is — routine, then the `taskScheduler.endpoints.default` key that points at it — with what each missing half reports.

3. **The fleet digest's shortlist filter knew only `[claudinite-task]`.** Every occurrence of every task in every member is `[claudinite-work]` now, and an item accumulates a comment per stage — so unfiltered they don't just appear in the brief, they win it, which is the exact failure the filter was written to prevent. It knows both; the test fails when either is dropped.

4. **`session_scope` lost its last reader and nothing said so.** `scheduled-tasks.md` still called it "deprecated, still honoured". Raised as an advisory rename (not a contract error — nothing converges a member's task files, so a member can't be migrated off it by a release) and dropped from the two canon tasks, which already declared the `invocation_endpoint` carrying their reach.

## The re-evaluations

**`packs/core/scheduled-tasks.md`** is the contract every task author reads and it described the slot machinery end to end. Rewritten: three responsibilities are tick/executor/janitor, the item's Context is the binding scope, the labels are the item's state, the lifecycle is the outcome labels. The **exclusive claim section is gone** — nothing has read `exclusive` since `run.mjs` went, and `after:` is the ordering it became. Added the prework-environment rule the new check enforces.

**Two lessons in the canon's local pack had gone from true to actively misleading**, and I corrected them in place rather than appending:
- *"exercise a task Action-side: move the slot hour and wait for the cron; a `workflow_dispatch` outside the window does nothing"* — the `wake` input is exactly how you do it now, and the drain picks it up in the same run.
- *"drive the real `planRun` from a non-due slot"* — `planRun` is deleted; the equivalent is `planTick` from a clock at which the anchor has not come.

Then the vocabulary itself across ~60 files: `dispatch issue` → work item, `ready-for-agent` → the queue's label set, "the scheduler runs the worker" → the executor runs prework, `slot` → anchor. `executor.md` stays but leads with a banner — a routine's prompt is console config no Action can rewrite, so deleting it breaks every routine not yet repointed, and the `update` task now checks for the queue instructions and reports what it found.

## Scoped out, filed

#994 — the usage fold's `tasks` **census** has no writer under the queue. `taskExec` is fine (that's the capture step, restored above). The census read job is different: each occurrence's outcome is an `outcome:*` label on its own item, which is a better record than log lines and a new read, not a repair. `task.md` and the fleet aggregate's own note now say the rows are historical, so nobody compares them against a later period and sees a fleet that stopped working.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

content.text:
Both are mine, added in this PR. Verified against the tree before answering.

## 1. `task-prework-env` on `packs/core/tasks/update/worker.mjs`

The new blocking check ([`packs/core/task-prework-env.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/slot-deletion-su0f1t/packs/core/task-prework-env.mjs)) says a task's code may read only the `CLAUDINITE_*` variables prework is handed. The update worker reads one more — `CLAUDINITE_CANON_REF` at [`worker.mjs:99`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/slot-deletion-su0f1t/packs/core/tasks/update/worker.mjs#L99).

It found this on its first real-tree run; I hadn't known about it. It is not the bug the rule hunts:

- **The variable has a live setter.** [`canary-rehearsal.yml:126`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/slot-deletion-su0f1t/.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml#L126) sets it, in this repo, beside the worker. The rule's failure mode is a channel whose *producer went away* — this one's producer is a file away.
- **Absence is the normal case, and handled.** `rehearsalRef` null is a real converge cycle; set, it clones the ref under test, reports, and restores the tree without branching or stamping. Under prework it is always null, which is the ordinary path.
- **The worker genuinely has two callers.** That's the same crossing the `barrier` entry four lines down already accepts, for the same reason: a release that changes the worker cannot be rehearsed by the canary's *vendored* copy, because that copy predates the release.

So the alternative to a waiver was weakening the rule for everyone, which would have cost more than it bought.

**One caveat you should know before approving it.** `applyConfig` matches an acceptance on `(rule, file path)` only — [`findings.mjs:23`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/slot-deletion-su0f1t/engine/checks/helpers/findings.mjs#L23) — there is no way to scope it to one finding inside a file. So this entry also silences any *future* stray `CLAUDINITE_*` read added to that same worker. Narrow file, unlikely, but real. The tighter alternative is to make the rule itself exempt a variable that a tracked workflow in the repo sets, and drop the waiver — a structural answer instead of a per-repo one. Say the word and I'll do that instead.

## 2. `reference-integrity` on `docs/task-prework/`

[`docs/task-prework/DESIGN.md:36`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/slot-deletion-su0f1t/docs/task-prework/DESIGN.md#L36) reads *"Two problems in the current staging (`engine/scheduler/run.mjs`)"* — and this PR deletes that module, so the reference dangles.

The fix is not to repoint it. That sentence names the staging the #405 migration **was changing**; pointing it at the queue's executor would make the document describe a design that never happened. The dangling is a true statement about a moment that has passed.

That is the standing this repo already gives the same shape — the `docs/per-project-scheduling/` entry directly below it says so in almost the same words, for the files migration #394 deleted. I put the new entry beside it deliberately, so the pattern reads as one rule rather than two exceptions.

Line 176 of the same file has a second such reference (`run.mjs` lines ~191–198); the subtree-scoped path covers both.

> ✅ Both explained and verified. The only open question is whether you want the `task-prework-env` waiver replaced by a structural exemption in the rule — say so and I'll swap it.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
